text.p: These are some of the main stories in Sofia newspapers today. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
-- Bulgaria's interim government is expected to liberalise fuel prices today.
-- The Union of Democratic Forces has won 52.26 percent in Saturday's elections and will have 137 seats in the 240-seat parliament, Bulgaria's Central Electoral Commission said.
-- Bulgaria needs $10 million to bridge fodder grain gap until the new harvest, Prime minister Stefan Sofianski said. @
-- Bulgaria's state forklift truck maker Balkankar said it would start talks with its creditors to reschedule company debts of some $40 million and six billion levs.
-- Bulgaria's Privatisation Agency said it had approved the sale of a 34 percent stake in the Sandanski Interhotel in southwestern Bulgaria for $4 million to the Bulgarian Tourist Holding.
-- Bulgaria's Black Sea holiday resorts have not suffered from recent costal landslides and are ready to welcome foreign tourists, Tourist Comittee chairman Roumen Draganov said. @

-- Bulgarian businessmen said at a seminar in Sofia the Value Added Tax, now 22 percent should be cut to six percent for basic goods and to 10 percent for other goods and services and corporate profit tax should be cut to 10 percent from 36 percent to boost the country's economic development.
-- The European bank for Reconstruction and Development is expected to buy a 35 percent stake in Bulgaria's copper smelter Pirdop, bank officials said.

-- Ivan Kostov, the leader of Bulgaria's reformist Union of Democratic Forces which won a clear majority in Saturday's elections, said he had invited a mission of the International Monetary Fund in May to complete reform preparations agreed in March.

-- The Bulgarian lev should not be pegged below 2,500 levs per dollar when a fixed exchange rate mechanism, a currency board system is introduced, because an overvalued lev would stifle Bulgarian exports, former Finance minister Stoyan Alexandrov said.
-- Bulgaria's caretaker cabinet is expected to raise salaries in the public sector by 38 percent from May 1. -- Sofia Newsroom, (++359-2) 981 8569
